did_you_know.text: Did you know? David captured Gath and its surrounding villages from the Philistines. Gath was a major Philistine city, and its capture is described as part of the subjugation of the Philistines.
Did you know? After defeating Moab, the chapter describes the Moabites as David’s servants and as tribute bearers—that is, they paid him tribute or brought him gifts as a sign of submission.
Did you know? The spoils David took from Hadadezer included one thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. He kept only one hundred of the chariots.

Did you know? After his victory over Aram-Damascus, David stationed garrisons there, and the chapter describes Aram as subject to him and bringing tribute. It also emphasizes that the Lord gave David victory wherever he went.
Did you know? David took a great quantity of bronze from Hadadezer’s cities. The chapter notes that Solomon later used this bronze to make the Bronze Sea, the pillars, and the bronze vessels.
Did you know? After Hadadezer’s defeat, Toi king of Hamath sent his son Hadoram to David to congratulate him and inquire about his welfare. The messenger brought articles of gold, silver, and bronze.
Did you know? David dedicated to the Lord the metal objects, silver, and gold he had taken from the nations, including Edom, Moab, Ammon, the Philistines, and Amalek.
Did you know? After Abishai son of Zeruiah defeated Edom in the Valley of Salt, David stationed garrisons throughout Edom, and the chapter describes Edom as subject to him.
Did you know? The chapter does not portray David’s reign solely through his wars. It emphasizes that David reigned over all Israel and administered justice and righteousness to all his people.
Did you know? David’s administration was well organized: Joab was commander of the army, Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder, Zadok and Abimelech were priests, and Shavsha was secretary.
